recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core source work is needed for FHIR-14850 unless the work group later reopens the broader policy for whole-batch rejection versus entry-level failures.
issue_request: FHIR-14850 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 FHIR-I change request asking for HTTP response-code guidance for batch. The final resolution clarified that a correctly processed batch has an overall 200 OK response regardless of individual operation success, and that individual statuses are found inside the returned Bundle.
initial_application: Jira comments cite svn revision 13373, and git-svn commit e867cdb92d42d005171704c48e7d9f15667aff1a applied GF#14850 to source/http.html by adding the batch response-code paragraph. That initial application added the requested 200 OK/returned-Bundle guidance; adjacent entry-failure wording was later corrected by FHIR-17776.
additional_context: source/http.html is active in the current build through source/hierarchy.xml. The current source says the overall batch HTTP response is 200 OK when the batch is processed correctly and tells readers to inspect the returned Bundle for interaction-level status. FHIR-17776 is already represented on the combined branch as an audit of the adjacent per-entry non-2xx failure wording. A 2021 Zulip implementers thread quoted and discussed the same rule without surfacing a conflicting decision, and Confluence searches found no FHIR-14850 references.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already matches the accepted FHIR-14850 rule, and adding 201, 207, or 4xx guidance from the reporter's proposal would conflict with the final resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later published issue corrected the adjacent entry-failure sentence while preserving the FHIR-14850 overall 200 OK batch guidance; it is already represented on the combined branch.
